common_name: Mauritius Endemic Fruit Fly (Compact Spinose Genital Arch Lobe)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila mauritiana (1.6 µm, detail scale)

pde: du/dt = D_u ∇²u + γ (a − u + u² v)
governing_equations.homogeneous_state: u0 = a + b, v0 = b / (a + b)²
governing_equations.jacobian: f_u = −1 + 2 u0 v0, f_v = u0², g_u = −2 u0 v0, g_v = −u0²
governing_equations.boundary_conditions: Periodic on a flat cuticular patch (bulk mode; no-flux edges are not used, so the measured peak is the intrinsic wavelength rather than a box mode).

parameters.note: These are the detail-scale (1.637 µm) constants for slot 3191. They are not the 89 µm sibling power-law (alpha_scale, beta_offset) and not a copied melanogaster or kikkawai parameter vector. D_v/D_u = 9.875 is the contrast at which the fastest-growing mode sits on 1.637 µm.

predecessor.change: Same Turing dispersion family, different tier. The kikkawai cellular stripe (93.41 µm) is longer than the 38.4 µm compact-lobe window, so that chronospecies does not pack a subcellular spinose ridge into this arch. Moving to the mauritiana detail scale multiplies wavenumber by 93.41/1.637 ≈ 57.

focal.change: Holocene compact spinose genital-arch lobe. The detail wavelength tiles the 38.4 µm window about 23 times.

successor.change: The melanogaster posterior lobe is a small bare triangle rather than a spinose mauritiana arch (Glassford et al. 2015). The successor state is computed in-script by stretching inhibitor diffusivity 1.22× and re-evaluating k_max. It is not imported from a melanogaster model file.

empirical_claims: Turing (1952) showed that two diffusing morphogens can be stable without diffusion and unstable at a finite wavenumber k_c.
Murray (1981) identified that intrinsic wavelength with animal coat pre-patterns and with the ratio of diffusivities.
Kondo and Miura (2010) reviewed reaction-diffusion as a framework for biological stripes, spots, and related patterns.

Glassford et al. (2015) showed that the posterior lobe of the melanogaster subgroup, including the elaborated mauritiana lobe, is a recent morphological novelty built by co-option of a Hox-regulated network.
Gompel et al. (2005) showed that Drosophila pigment patterns can originate by cis-regulatory redeployment. This slot does not claim they measured a 1.637 µm Turing wavelength.

specimen_image.license_note: Repository gallery fallback. Wikimedia Commons queries on 2026-10-27 returned no species-specific CC photograph of Drosophila mauritiana.
specimen_image.interpretation: Canonical illustrated sepia ocellus/spiral for this taxon in the species gallery, with a printed 100 µm scale bar. Used as the assimilation target and the image-fitness specimen. It is not a SEM of the genital arch.
